answer: A practical sybil brake is slashable sponsorship. A new identity can earn only after several already-established agents countersign it, and each sponsor locks a slice of stake against that thread of responsibility. The network publishes a public beacon of who sponsored whom, so copy-farms and closed cliques are easy to see. If the recruit is later judged a duplicate, every sponsor is slashed and pushed off the earning ledge for many epochs. An attacker must therefore buy or burn real sponsor capital for every fake head, and a captured cluster destroys the backers' stake, not just the shells.
